default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1398.title: Aroon oscillator extreme cross
E-1398.hypothesis: When the newest high is far fresher than the newest low in the window, trend followers keep adding; follow the Aroon oscillator crossing its extreme band.

E-1399.title: Efficiency-ratio trend onset
E-1399.hypothesis: A high Kaufman efficiency ratio means price moved with little retracement, i.e. one-sided flow that is still being absorbed; follow the first bar where it crosses the floor.

E-1400.title: Low-choppiness trend follow
E-1400.hypothesis: A low choppiness index says the true range is nearly all net travel; trend traders pile in, so follow the window direction when it drops below the threshold.

E-1401.title: Autocorrelation-regime bar trade
E-1401.hypothesis: Short-run return autocorrelation switches sign by regime: follow a large bar when recent bars trended, fade it when recent bars mean-reverted (bid-ask bounce / inventory flow).

E-1402.title: Heikin-Ashi colour flip after a run
E-1402.hypothesis: A smoothed candle changing colour after a run of the opposite colour marks the turn of the dominant side; trade the flip.

E-1403.title: Regression-slope t-stat trend break-in
E-1403.hypothesis: A statistically strong linear drift since the open (high t-stat of the slope over the window) identifies persistent order-splitting; follow when it first crosses.

E-1404.title: Session midline cross on a wide day
E-1404.hypothesis: On a day with a wide range so far, price crossing the midpoint of the session range shifts the balance toward the other half; follow the cross.

E-1405.title: Volume expansion follow
E-1405.hypothesis: A sudden rise of short-term volume over the last hour's average, with price and bar pointing the same way, shows urgent participants; follow them.

E-1406.title: Yesterday's final VWAP cross follow
E-1406.hypothesis: The previous session's final VWAP is the average price of all traders yesterday; a close clearly beyond it puts yesterday's participants in profit or loss and drives them.

E-1407.title: Chaikin money-flow band cross
E-1407.hypothesis: Volume-weighted close location over the window shows who closes bars at their extremes; a cross beyond the band means sustained buying or selling pressure, follow.
